text:
Faye: quick sync  ran a new probe for 'coherence-window backpressure' on ember-20b-quant (GPTQ4) to see if we can keep speculative prefetch wins while avoiding the multi-step collapse we've been seeing.
Owen: what's the high-level idea?
Faye: instead of fixed prefetch size, we monitor a rolling "coherence score" over the last N tokens (combines token-entropy trend + top1_prob stability). if coherence drops below a threshold we apply backpressure: reduce prefetch, raise accept_threshold, and force a short KV re-warm.
Diego: interesting. how cheap is the coherence calc?
Faye: incremental stats only (mean, stddev, delta) so essentially free at runtime. implemented as 6-token sliding window.
Rhea: experiment matrix?
Faye: 6k prompts stratified: short/mid/long. arms: baseline=gptq4 greedy; A=static-sampler (prefetch=32, accept=0.6); B=coherence-backpressure (prefetch adaptive 8-32, accept adaptive 0.6-0.8); C=int8 baseline for comparison. temp=0.7.
Owen: numbers?
Faye: p50 token latency: baseline 160ms, A 110ms, B 118ms. longform ROUGE-L delta: A -1.9, B -0.7. trivia EM: A -2.6, B -0.9. int8 baseline closed ~1.1 EM vs gptq4 baseline but +9% latency.
Diego: coherence-backpressure seems promising. CI?
Faye: 95% bootstrap CI on longform ROUGE for B: [-1.2, -0.3]. for A: [-2.5, -1.3].
Rhea: any illustrative diffs?
Faye: example:
PROMPT: "Prepare a step-by-step migration checklist for user profiles including verification and rollback."
BASELINE: explicit 6-step checklist with verification commands and rollback steps.
ARM A (static): compresses items 3-5 into a single paraphrase and omits explicit rollback command.
ARM B (coherence-backpressure): preserves checklist items; wording slightly terser but keeps rollback.
NOTES: backpressure kicked in mid-checklist and forced a KV re-warm which preserved explicit tokens.
Owen: did you record where backpressure triggered? useful for routing heuristics.
Faye: yes  primarily triggered on mid-long contexts with entropy spikes after procedural verbs or entity tokens. we logged trigger_count, prefetch_at_trigger, and kv_rewarm_performed.
Diego: quant interaction? int8+backpressure?
Faye: quick int8+backpressure mini-run: int8+backpressure recovered most EM loss (within 0.4 of baseline) but latency advantage reduced ~6% vs gptq4+backpressure. tradeoff depends on cost model.
Rhea: rollout plan / guardrails?
Faye: propose staged: 1) run 12k stratified on staging comparing baseline, static-sampler, backpressure, and int8+backpressure; 2) surface top-400 diffs for blind human eval; 3) route rule: if prompt_len>220 OR ner_count>3 -> bias towards backpressure (more conservative); 4) autopilot: rollback if cohort ROUGE drops >0.8 or trivia EM drops >1.0.
Owen: config snippet?
Faye: paste config: {"sampler":"adaptive","coherence_window":6,"entropy_threshold":1.1,"top1_stability_threshold":0.12,"prefetch_range":[8,32],"accept_bounds":[0.6,0.8],"kv_rewarm":"on_trigger"}
Diego: please include accept_rate, trigger_count, kv_rewarm_rate, top1_prob_drop, and per-token entropy in outputs. also compute per-session $ estimate via Redwood Optimize.
Rhea: agree. add human eval for the top disagreements and include a quick taxonomy: "missing-step", "wrong-detail", "stylistic".
Faye: noted. starting the 12k run on staging tomorrow morning, expect ~20h. eval-bot: scheduled job "coherence-backpressure-ember-2026-03-24" -> staging (job id: 13121)
Owen: one more ask  if backpressure triggers >2x for a prompt, mark that prompt as "high-risk" and exclude from sampler cohort until manual review.
Faye: will do and dump those to /mnt/holdouts/coherence_backpressure_risks_2026.
Diego: great. if results hold, we can add a small conservative lane to prod routing and let Redwood Optimize recommend quant+batch knobs for each lane.
Rhea: thanks Faye 44D keep the diffs coming.
Faye: will post the summary + top diffs when job completes.
